gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the cooled UGREEN MagFlow Pro car mount has an independent charging test: Gizmodo Japan (SUMA-KIYO, 2026-08-29) charged an iPhone 17 Pro from 20% to 74% in 30 minutes and 95% in 60 minutes on it, against 61% and 86% on UGREEN's uncooled MagFlow 25W mount in the same car with the A/C on low.
standout_why: I checked MobileReviews Eh! (cited in two chats), mobileplustech, Macworld's car-charger roundup, Macworld's MagSafe roundup (updated 2026-11-12), Macworld's Anker Prime car charger review, iOS Hacker, Tiny Tech Box and iPhoner. Neither the UGREEN MagFlow Pro nor any UGREEN mount with TEC cooling appears in any test. MobileReviews' three UGREEN entries are the uncooled MagFlow 55967, the WM701 suction-cup mount and the W778. In three chats ChatGPT said it had found no independent sustained-speed test for UGREEN, yet it still made UGREEN its value pick. Mobileplustech and Tiny Tech Box say outright that they did no hands-on testing. Macworld's Anker review has no measured figures, only an expected 'just over half an hour' to 50% and Anker's below-35 °C claim, so ChatGPT's 'Macworld's recent testing identifies the Anker Prime as one of the fastest' rests on no published measurement. Not new: MobileReviews' measurement of the Anker A2933 at 11.7 W into the battery with 38.5% efficiency, ninth of the nine mounts that charged, is in a page ChatGPT cited, although no ChatGPT answer ever repeated it.
decides: Our page can be the only one with named measurements for all three of ChatGPT's recurring picks. On MobileReviews' 30-minute rig (iPhone 17 Pro starting near 15%, Apple 140 W supply), ESR OmniLock averaged 19.1 W into the battery with a 35.3 °C peak mount surface, and Anker Prime A2933 averaged 11.7 W at 37.4 °C. Gizmodo Japan measured UGREEN MagFlow Pro adding 54 points in 30 minutes, 13 more than UGREEN's uncooled mount. That makes ESR the measured pick for sustained speed. Anker's 'premium/strongest cooling' slot is not supported by the one independent number, which is the slowest working result in that test. UGREEN gains evidence for its cooling, but the two tests used different methods, so its numbers cannot be ranked against ESR's.
